overview: AMP Limited is an Australian and New Zealand wealth management, superannuation and banking group operating through five business units: Platforms (the North investment platform), Superannuation & Investments (AMP Super master trust), New Zealand Wealth Management (KiwiSaver, retail investments, enable.me advice), AMP Bank (residential mortgages, deposits, AMP Bank GO digital bank), and Partnerships & Group (minority stakes in China Life Pension Company, China Life AMP Asset Management, PCCP and Akumin). AMP has repositioned itself as a capital-light retirement specialist after divesting AMP Life (2020-21), AMP Capital and its Advice business, returning over $1.1bn of capital to shareholders and resuming dividends in FY2024/25.

business_model.summary: Revenue is earned mainly as asset-based fees on AUM held on the North platform and in AMP Super (recurring, scales with markets and net flows), net interest income from AMP Bank's mortgage and deposit book, and equity-accounted profit shares from Asian and US partnerships. Post-divestment, FY2019-2021 statutory results are not comparable to the current, much smaller and more capital-light group; management now reports Underlying NPAT as its headline measure alongside statutory profit, which still carries below-the-line remediation, simplification and one-off items.

revenue_streams.name: Other revenue (Advice retained interest, NZ non-AUM lines, guarantees)

business_model.customer_type: B2C mass-affluent pre-retirees and retirees, distributed via independent financial advisers (B2B2C) in Australia and NZ, plus direct-to-consumer digital banking (AMP Bank GO)
business_model.geographic_mix: Australia (majority of Platforms, Superannuation & Investments, AMP Bank), New Zealand (Wealth Management/KiwiSaver), plus non-controlling equity interests in China (CLPC, CLAMP) and the US (PCCP, Akumin)

main_competitors: Insignia Financial (now owned by CC Capital)
Industry/mega super funds (AustralianSuper, Australian Retirement Trust)
competitive_position.market_position: One of the larger retail wealth platforms and master trusts in Australia via North and AMP Super, but has lost significant share since the 2018 Royal Commission and is a sub-scale niche/challenger bank; competing against both listed platform specialists (Netwealth, HUB24) and much larger industry super funds that are increasingly moving into retail-style advice and retirement products

moat_factors.factor: Adviser network and platform switching costs
moat_factors.description: North's retirement-focused functionality (Lifetime Income, Guarantees, Managed Portfolios) and entrenched adviser relationships create some stickiness, evidenced by 122 net new advisers activated and 65 new AFSL distribution agreements in FY25
One of the largest retail Master Trusts in Australia gives scale economics versus smaller platforms, though industry super funds are larger still
MyNorth Lifetime/Deferred Lifetime Income and guarantee products are a differentiated retirement-income offer relative to accumulation-focused industry funds

Reputation was severely damaged by the 2018 Royal Commission; company reports reputation (Reptrak score) has recovered to its highest level since 2008 but trust remains a lingering weakness versus industry super funds
Minority stakes (CLPC 19.99%, CLAMP 14.97%) provide diversified, high-growth earnings uncorrelated with the Australian wealth cycle, but AMP has no operational control

weaknesses: Sub-scale versus mega industry super funds and big-4 banks, limiting cost leverage
AMP Bank is a minor player with modest NIM (~1.25-1.28%) and negative-to-low returns on capital while AMP Bank GO scales up
History of legacy legal/remediation matters continues to produce below-the-line statutory charges
Superannuation & Investments only achieved its first positive net cashflow half in FY26 after outflows since 2017, reflecting a still-fragile retention position
No control over Partnerships & Group earnings, which are a meaningful and volatile share of profit

growth_drivers: Accelerating growth in wealth businesses: adviser activations, managed portfolios (North Managed Portfolios AUM $25.2bn FY25, $28.3bn 1H26) and North Interactive platform launch
Retirement product innovation (MyNorth Lifetime, Deferred Lifetime Income, North Guarantees, AMP Super Lifetime, digital advice journeys) targeting Australia's ageing, ~$4.4tn+ superannuation pool
AMP Bank GO digital bank scaling deposits/customers to diversify funding and target underserved mini-business and personal segments (guidance of $2.0bn total deposits)
AI adoption (AI Filenote, North modelling tools, 'AI Implement') to lift adviser productivity and cut controllable costs
Turning Superannuation & Investments to sustained positive net cashflows via member retention, digital advice and AMP Super Lifetime/Rewards
Capital-light strategy: continuing on-market buybacks (up to $300m in 2026), capital release from AMP Bank, and increasing dividends from China/US partnerships

Optionality on inorganic growth/consolidation in a fragmenting wealth platform and advice market (reported interest in Insignia Financial, since acquired by CC Capital) and 'intersection of wealth and property' product exploration

business.risk: Competitive intensity from platform specialists and mega super funds
business.description: Netwealth/HUB24 compete on platform technology and fees; AustralianSuper and other industry funds are moving into retail-style advice under DBFO reforms, competing directly for retirement flows
AUM-based revenue margins have been declining across segments (Platforms 45bps FY24 to 41bps 1H26; Super & Investments 63bps to 60bps) due to fee caps, AUM growth mix and tiered fee structures
Investment in the new digital bank is currently earnings-dilutive (AMP Bank NPAT down 33% in 1H26) and depends on successfully building deposits and customer numbers
Partnerships & Group (China Life, PCCP, Akumin) is a large and volatile swing factor in underlying NPAT (from $2m to $43m half-on-half) that AMP does not control

financial.description: Statutory NPAT continues to be materially below underlying NPAT due to business simplification costs, litigation/remediation and permanent tax differences ($152m of below-NPAT items in FY25)

financial.risk: Corporate debt and capital markets access
financial.description: Corporate debt reduced to $475m after redeeming $275m of AT1 notes; interest expense remains a drag on Partnerships & Group earnings
New Zealand Wealth Management earnings are translated at AUD/NZD rates that have moved unfavourably in recent periods (-$2m impact in 1H26)

regulatory.description: Delivering Better Financial Outcomes Tranche 2 reforms (intra-fund advice charging, targeted prompts, New Class of Adviser) could reshape how advice is delivered and monetised across the industry, creating both risk and opportunity
AMP Bank, N.M. Superannuation (RSE licensee) and AFSL-licensed wealth businesses face capital, liquidity and operational resilience requirements, plus AML-CTF reform and uplift obligations

regulatory.risk: Best financial interests duty and investment/product governance
regulatory.description: Ongoing regulatory focus on trustee accountability and member outcomes increases compliance costs for master trust and platform businesses
Financial services conduct remains a high-focus area post-Royal Commission; any recurrence of conduct failures would be reputationally costly given AMP's history

macro.description: AUM-based revenue and NPAT are directly linked to equity market performance; management explicitly notes 2025 results were supported by strong (especially US) equity markets
AMP Bank's net interest margin (~1.25-1.28%) is sensitive to RBA rate settings, funding costs and mortgage competition; NIM guided broadly flat around 1.25%

macro.risk: Australian/NZ economic conditions and cost-of-living pressures
macro.description: Management cites persistent cost-of-living pressures and challenging NZ economic conditions affecting customer saving/investing behaviour and mortgage demand

macro.risk: Cyber security, financial crime, fraud and scams
macro.description: Identified as a top material risk given the digital banking and platform footprint; ongoing investment required to keep pace with evolving threats

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Australian superannuation assets exceed A$4.4 trillion (RBA projects ~A$8.1tn by 2035), with structural tailwinds from compulsory super, an ageing population, and rising household wealth; DBFO advice reforms and intensifying competition from very large industry ('mega') super funds are reshaping distribution and advice economics
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderately cyclical - AUM-based revenue and investment income are exposed to equity market cycles; banking earnings are exposed to the Australian/NZ mortgage and rate cycle
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate - AMP Bank NIM and funding costs move with RBA cash rate and wholesale funding markets; Group investment income also benefits from higher rates on cash holdings

recent_developments.event: 1H26 results: statutory NPAT $154m (+57% YoY), underlying NPAT $174m (+33%), underlying EPS 6.9cps (+32.7%), RoE (underlying) 9.8%; interim dividend of 3.0cps (20% franked) declared; shares rallied ~6% toward 52-week highs on the print
Board approved a second $150m tranche of on-market share buybacks, bringing total FY26 buyback capacity to $300m; capital surplus (CET1) rose to $322m
Superannuation & Investments recorded its first half of positive net cashflows ($76m) since 2017, a key turnaround milestone
Blair Vernon (former CFO) formally became CEO and Managing Director (appointed 30 March 2026), succeeding Alexis George who retired after ~5 years leading AMP's post-Royal Commission transformation

FY25 results: underlying NPAT $285m (+20.8%), underlying EPS 11.3cps (+25.6%), statutory NPAT $133m (-11.3%); FY25 total dividend 4.0cps (20% franked), resuming a full-year payout; controllable costs down 6.9% to $603m
AMP announced Blair Vernon's appointment as incoming CEO, effective following Alexis George's retirement

Insignia Financial (a major wealth management/platform competitor) agreed to a ~A$3.3bn takeover by CC Capital at A$4.80/share, completing the sector consolidation; AMP was earlier reported as having considered interest in Insignia
AMP Bank GO, AMP's new digital bank targeting mini-business and personal customers, launched; by FY25 it had reached $310m in deposits and 15,665 customers

items.notes: Management increased guidance on target returns across the capital-light investment portfolio, signalling confidence in capital allocation discipline
Reflects structural funding mix shift toward AMP Bank GO and further securitisation
Deposits were $310m at FY25 and continuing to scale through 2026
Reflects continued fee-cap and AUM-growth mix pressure
Consistent margin compression trend flagged by management
Preferred method of returning excess capital to shareholders over the medium term

guidance.management_commentary: New CEO Blair Vernon described the 1H26 result as reflecting 'genuine momentum and operating leverage' in AMP's wealth businesses. Strategic priorities under Vernon are: (1) accelerating growth in wealth businesses (advisers, cashflows, retirement product innovation), (2) increasing business cash generation and returns to shareholders (dividends from partnerships, capital release from AMP Bank, buybacks), and (3) leveraging AI while managing emerging cyber and fiscal risks. The Board will review the FY26 final dividend later in the year.

bull_case: Underlying earnings momentum is clearly re-accelerating (underlying NPAT +20.8% FY25, +32.8% 1H26) with cost discipline (controllable costs down 6.9% in FY25) driving positive operating leverage
Superannuation & Investments turned cashflow-positive for the first time since 2017, removing a long-standing drag and de-risking the largest legacy weak spot in the portfolio
Capital-light, buyback-heavy capital allocation (up to $300m in 2026, plus a resumed and growing dividend) directly supports EPS growth and total shareholder return (16.7% TSR in FY25)

Structural tailwinds from a >$4.4tn and growing Australian superannuation pool, an ageing population needing retirement income solutions, and AMP's differentiated retirement product suite (North Guarantees, Lifetime Income, Managed Portfolios) position it well in a market undergoing consolidation

China Life Pension Company and other partnership stakes provide a fast-growing, largely uncorrelated earnings stream (China contribution +53-107% YoY in recent periods) that requires no incremental AMP capital
bear_case: Statutory profit remains persistently well below underlying profit due to recurring one-off, remediation and simplification charges, raising questions about the durability/quality of the 'underlying' earnings narrative
AUM-based revenue margins are structurally declining across every wealth segment (fee caps, tiered pricing, AUM mix), meaning revenue growth depends on volume/markets outrunning margin compression

AMP remains sub-scale versus both digital-native platform rivals (Netwealth, HUB24) and Australia's very large industry ('mega') super funds, which are now pushing into retail-style advice under DBFO reform, intensifying competitive pressure from both ends
AMP Bank GO is dilutive to Bank earnings today (Bank NPAT -33% in 1H26) with no guarantee the digital deposit strategy reaches profitable scale before competitive/funding pressures bite

Business remains heavily geared to equity market strength (AUM-based fees, investment income) and reputational fragility post-Royal Commission means any renewed conduct or cyber/fraud incident could disproportionately damage trust and flows
